# contentful_preview_environment (Resource)

Manages a Contentful content preview platform. This space-level resource is not a Contentful environment.

## Content preview configuration

This resource manages preview platforms under **Settings → Content preview** in Contentful, including their content type preview URLs. Manage custom preview tokens with [`contentful_live_preview_variables`](live_preview_variables).

Use Contentful's [content preview setup guide](https://www.contentful.com/developers/docs/tutorials/preview/content-preview/) for URL placeholders and frontend requirements. Preview URLs are stored in Terraform state; keep credentials out of them.

## Configuration lifecycle

Terraform manages active configurations as a map keyed by content type ID. Removing a key disables its configuration in Contentful. Setting the map to `{}` disables all configurations previously managed by this resource. Adding a key again enables that content type with the configured URL. Disabled remote configurations remain hidden during refresh and import.

## Selected IDs and replacement

Omit `preview_environment_id` to let Contentful assign an ID. To manage an existing platform, import it first. Selected-ID creation uses the same Contentful endpoint as updates and can modify an existing platform with version `0`.

When replacing a platform that has had configurations, choose a new selected ID. Observed Contentful behavior can prevent configuration under a reused ID even after deletion. Do not use `create_before_destroy` with the same selected ID: the create request can update the old platform before Terraform deletes it.

## Example Usage

Use either a Contentful-generated ID or an ID you select:

```terraform
resource "contentful_preview_environment" "this" {
  space_id    = var.contentful_space_id
  name        = "Website preview"
  description = "Draft website"

  content_type_configurations = {
    page = {
      url = "https://preview.example.com/{env_id}/pages/{entry.sys.id}"
    }
    article = {
      url = "https://preview.example.com/{env_id}/articles/{entry.fields.slug}"
    }
  }
}

resource "contentful_preview_environment" "selected_id" {
  space_id               = var.contentful_space_id
  preview_environment_id = var.preview_environment_id
  name                   = "Website preview with selected ID"

  content_type_configurations = {
    page = {
      url = "https://preview.example.com/{env_id}/pages/{entry.sys.id}"
    }
  }
}
```

## Concurrent edits and recovery

Updates use Contentful's last observed version. Configuration-only changes have been observed not to advance that version, so version checks cannot protect against concurrent edits to the same preview URL.

If a write returns values that differ from the plan, the provider records the returned values in state and reports a consistency error. Inspect the preview platform, then refresh and review the next plan before applying again.

If Contentful returns an unsupported or ambiguous active configuration, refresh warns and omits that entry while retaining the configurations it can represent. Resolve the reported configuration in Contentful before applying again.

## Schema

### Required

- `content_type_configurations` (Attributes Map) Active preview URL configurations keyed by content type ID. Removing a key disables its configuration; an empty map disables all managed configurations. Reads and imports omit disabled configurations. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--content_type_configurations))
- `name` (String) Name of the content preview platform.
- `space_id` (String) ID of the space containing the content preview platform. Changing this value replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the content preview platform. Defaults to an empty string.
- `preview_environment_id` (String) System ID of the content preview platform. Omit to let Contentful generate an ID. Selected IDs accept 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores; changing a configured ID replaces the resource.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite Terraform resource identifier in `space_id/preview_environment_id` form.

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Timeout for the complete operation, including retries, such as `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`.
- `delete` (String) Timeout for the complete operation, including retries, such as `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`. Uses the value saved in state, with a minimum of `10s`.
- `read` (String) Timeout for the complete operation, including retries, such as `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`. Uses the value saved in state, with a minimum of `10s`.
- `update` (String) Timeout for the complete operation, including retries, such as `30s` or `5m`. Defaults to `2m`.

## Import

Import uses the space ID and preview environment ID. Only active content type configurations enter Terraform state. The examples target the generated-ID resource `contentful_preview_environment.this`; change the address if managing the selected-ID example.

### Import by identity

Terraform 1.12 or later:

```terraform
import {
  identity = {
    space_id               = var.contentful_space_id
    preview_environment_id = var.preview_environment_id
  }
  to = contentful_preview_environment.this
}
```

### Import by ID

Terraform 1.5 or later:

```terraform
import {
  id = "${var.contentful_space_id}/${var.preview_environment_id}"
  to = contentful_preview_environment.this
}
```

### Import with the CLI

Set the shell variables to your Contentful IDs:

```shell
terraform import contentful_preview_environment.this "$CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID/$CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_ENVIRONMENT_ID"
```
